title: Atomic cutover saga with user-affinity handshake and autocorrect rollbacks
author: Jordan Kim
description: Context: Large customer deployments exposed a race in session-affine canary cutovers where user sessions were split between old and new models during a multi-step promote, causing degraded UX and noisy SLO alerts. This PR implements a coordinated, transactional cutover 'saga' that preserves session affinity, stages user cohort handshakes, and provides an autocorrect rollback pathway when safety checks fail. Motivation: Reduce user-visible flapping during promotions, make rollbacks fast and explainable, and provide operators a deterministic playbook for cross-region cutovers. Design highlights: 1) AtomicCutoverSaga controller — a new orchestration primitive that sequences probe -> handshake -> promote -> verification steps with checkpointed progress so rollbacks are deterministic. Each step emits provenance metadata for audit and replay. 2) UserAffinityProxy — lightweight routing layer that pins active sessions to the pre-cutover model until the handshake completes; supports sticky cookies and token-based leases for API clients. 3) AutocorrectRollback policy — rule engine that evaluates multi-metric windows (latency, error-rate, semantic-drift score) and triggers a staged rollback which can be automatically promoted to a fast revert if thresholds are still breached. 4) Telemetry signals and human-in-the-loop hooks — emits a 'cutover.trace' span with decision reasons to the tracing backend and surfaces a single-click abort/rollback action in the Console. Backwards compatibility: New defaults are opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers; Hosted uses gradual rollout for the first 30 days. Checklist: - [x] Implement AtomicCutoverSaga controller and unit tests - [x] Add UserAffinityProxy and integration test harness - [x] AutocorrectRollback policy + policy params in rollout CRD - [x] Tracing + Console button wiring - [x] E2E smoke tests against canary harness - [x] Docs: playbook and runbook snippets - [x] Release notes Draft Changeset summary: - New CRD: RolloutSaga (spec for staged cutover steps, metrics, abort windows) - Controller: controllers/rollout_saga.go (core logic, checkpointing) - Router: router/user_affinity_proxy.go (session pinning, lease renewal) - Policy: rollback/autocorrect_engine.go (multi-metric evaluator) - Console: ui/rollouts/atomic-cutover-button.tsx (abort/promote actions) - Telemetry: tracing/cutover_traces.go (span enrichment) - Tests: integration/atomic_cutover_test.go, e2e/cutover_smoke.sh Security & privacy: affinity token is TTL-bound and encrypted; no user PII is logged. Operational notes: - Default autopilot is disabled for tenants with strict change control (can be toggled in Console). - Operators can opt into 'strict verification' mode which requires manual approval between handshake and promote. Rollout plan: staged rollout for Hosted customers starting with 5% of traffic for 24h, escalate to 25% if verification passes, final promote after 72h. Dedicated customers can enable immediately after scheduling a maintenance window. Related work: builds on the checkpointed promote model from ENG-1910 and shadow handoff work in SUP-992. Testing & validation: ran 3 production-like canary rehearsals in benchmark-lab; autocorrect rollback triggered correctly on injected latency and semantic-drift faults. Known limitations: - Cross-region session stickiness requires sticky token propagation (future work: distributed lease coordinator). - Very large burst traffic patterns may require additional pre-warming of caches; documented as mitigation.

release_notes: Introduces RolloutSaga (atomic cutover orchestration) with session affinity proxy and an autocorrect rollback policy. Admins can opt into automatic rollback or require manual verification. See docs/playbooks/atomic-cutover.md for runbook and Console operator actions.
notes_for_ops: Operators: monitor cutover.trace spans and the new metrics rollout.saga.step_duration_seconds and rollback.autocorrect.triggers. Use Console single-click abort if the automated rollback is disabled. For Dedicated clusters, schedule a maintenance window when enabling strict verification.
playbook_snippet: 1) Start RolloutSaga in dry-run mode for a small cohort. 2) Verify handshake metrics (handshake.latency < 200ms, handshake.failures == 0). 3) Promote to 25% and monitor grouped metrics for 2h. 4) If autocorrect triggers, follow audit log to replay decision and escalate to manual abort if needed.
